title: notification-02: Store + Lifecycle
summary: Store app-owned, queue, dedup, expiry e scheduling timer.
description: NotificationStore (next_id, notifications, dedup_index, queued, visible[4], history FIFO bounded da history_limit), NotificationRuntime (store + proprio Signal<Vec<ToastSpec>>), expiry nel lifecycle loop con ControlFlow::WaitUntil(next_expiry).
goals: NotificationStore con push/dismiss/lookup azione/expiry/dedup/policy di visibilita, integrato nel lifecycle loop senza busy-loop.
nonGoals: Task separato per la history bounded: gia coperta dagli invarianti di NotificationStore stesso (T198), non serve una voce a parte (l'ex 252SA del branch abbandonato e superflua).
completionCriteria: NotificationStore + NotificationRuntime scritti e verificati con cargo check (fatto)
expiry cablata nel lifecycle loop con wake scheduling corretto (fatto)
history_limit letto da [settings].notification_system invece di un placeholder hardcoded (non fatto, dipende da T186/T191)

Questo primitivo per-id è quello che l'azione `NotificationDismissOne` (P059) chiama direttamente; `NotificationDismissAll`/`NotificationDismissLast` iterano lo store chiamandolo per ciascun id idoneo — nessuna logica duplicata a livello WmAction.

tasks.title: Implement visible toast policy
tasks.description:
Produrre lista visibile di `ToastSpec`; v1 max_visible=4, sticky/danger prioritari, poi più recenti.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED (pre-existing in the ported heca/src/notification.rs): MAX_VISIBLE_NOTIFICATIONS=4 stable slots; promote_pending() fills a vacant slot from the front of the FIFO queue. DEVIATION from this task's original policy text ("sticky/danger prioritari, poi più recenti"): the actual shipped policy is pure FIFO promotion order, no severity/stickiness-based reordering or priority queue — "existing visible entries never reorder" is a documented invariant. This is a real simplification from the original spec, not an oversight; flagging in case severity-priority promotion is still wanted as a follow-up. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean; unit tests cover slot stability. FILES: heca/src/notification.rs.

tasks.title: Schedule next notification expiry
tasks.description:
Esporre `next_expiry()` e usarla per `ControlFlow::WaitUntil` quando non c'è animazione più urgente.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: NotificationStore::next_expiry() (pre-existing, min of visible entries' expires_at) exposed via NotificationRuntime::next_expiry(). Wired into app/lifecycle.rs's handle_about_to_wait this session: when nothing else needs continuous polling (no ongoing animation), falls back to ControlFlow::WaitUntil(next_expiry) instead of plain Wait — so the app wakes exactly once at the deadline rather than busy-polling. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. FILES: heca/src/notification.rs, heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs.

tasks.title: Integrate expiry in lifecycle loop
tasks.description:
Chiamare expiry da `handle_about_to_wait`, marcare redraw solo su cambio e non busy-loopare.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs's handle_about_to_wait calls state.notifications.expire_due(Instant::now()) each frame; only sets state.needs_redraw when it returns true (a real change), no unconditional redraw. Combined with T201's WaitUntil(next_expiry), this does not busy-loop — the app sleeps until the next actual deadline instead of polling every frame. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. NOT verified: no running app yet to observe the actual wake cadence. FILES: heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs.
